body:
~The persist flag is for saving scenes, and doesn't matter for duplication~ documentation was incomplete 

Does this happen when using GDScript and using a lambda function? If it does then this is likely a limitation with how C# delegate callables are duplicated

Also does it work with other syntax like:
```cs
button.Connect("pressed", Callable.From(() => GD.Print("pressed")))
```

> The persist flag is for saving scenes, and doesn't matter for duplication

Mmm, no. Just for clarity, it absolutely **does** matter:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/65618
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99631

Confirmed on 4.4.1.stable.mono.

The issue does _not_ occur for me with GDScript, as long as `CONNECT_PERSIST` is passed to the connect function (this is missing in the snippet above).

Two of the C# variations give an error:

```csharp
        button.Connect("pressed", Callable.From(Pressed), (uint)ConnectFlags.Persist);

        button.Connect("pressed", Callable.From(() => Pressed()), (uint)ConnectFlags.Persist);
```
both give:

cc @AThousandShips

I have a similar issue in 4.6.1.stable in GDScript with a child node. Not sure if this would require a new issue, since the title would _almost_ look the same:
"Signals created with GodotObject.Connect() aren't on the duplicated **child** node when using Node.Duplicate()."

1. Node 'A' has a child node with a connected signal (persist flag on)
2. I duplicate 'A', let's call it 'B'
3. the child of 'B' does not have the same signal connected as the child of 'A'.

This is with the duplicate_signals flag set.

This works:

```csharp
button.Connect(Button.SignalName.Pressed, new Callable(this, MethodName.Pressed), (uint)ConnectFlags.Persist);
```

So, as @AThousandShips suspected, this seems to be a limitation of how C# delegate callables are duplicated.

However, looking at GDScript, it looks like it doesn't work for lambdas either:

```gdscript
button.connect("pressed", func(): print("pressed"), CONNECT_PERSIST)
```

I'm guessing, `duplicate` just doesn't work for any `CallableCustom` type.
